message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy within your mandate. The business looks fundamentally sound: total net sales were $391,035 million (up 2% year over year), with Services growing 13% to $96,169 million at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123,216 million and operating cash flow was strong at $118,254 million. Net income dipped to $93,736 million (diluted EPS $6.08) primarily because of a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision — the operating trend, not operations, drove the decline — and the balance sheet holds roughly $140 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Key watch items are the 8% Greater China sales decline to $66,952 million and ongoing DMA/DOJ antitrust matters. With the quote at $222.70, I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (about $9,803, under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit; the order filled at $222.80). This is a buy-only, cash-funded purchase using existing account cash — no funds were moved out — and it leaves room for a possible MSFT order later today if warranted.
